Playbook.name: Windows — PowerShell Engine Downgraded to v2 (AMSI and Script-Block-Logging Bypass) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: PowerShell ran with engine version 2.x (events 400/403/4103) - PowerShell v2 predates AMSI and script-block logging, so attackers force a downgrade to evade both. Triage question: is this an evasion downgrade to run unmonitored code, or a legacy app genuinely needing v2?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A v2 downgrade blinds AMSI and script-block logging, letting malicious PowerShell run undetected.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the PowerShell v2 downgrade is an evasion attempt or a legacy-application requirement.

Step.name: Confirm the v2 engine start and its host/user
Step.Purpose: Establish where and by whom v2 was invoked - a forced downgrade on a modern host is suspicious.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.powershell_operational-*,logs-windows.powershell-* | WHERE event.code IN ("400","403","4103") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND powershell.engine.version LIKE "2.*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, powershell.engine.version, user.name, host.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A v2 start on a host that has no legacy-app reason is a deliberate downgrade (powershell -version 2). Note the user - a normal/service account forcing v2 is evasion.

Step.name: What ran under the v2 session
Step.Purpose: v2 is chosen to run something unmonitored - look for the process/network activity around it.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)(powershell|pwsh).*" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE cl LIKE "*-version 2*" OR cl LIKE "*-v 2*" | KEEP @timestamp, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A -version 2 flag confirms a forced downgrade. The parent and any additional arguments show intent. Because v2 bypasses script-block logging, correlate with process/network telemetry rather than PowerShell logs.

Node.Condition: A deliberate v2 downgrade (-version 2) on a modern host by an unexpected account, especially with suspicious activity.
A documented legacy application that requires PowerShell v2.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-PSV2-START, INV-02-PSV2-ACTIVITY to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A legacy application legitimately requiring PowerShell v2.

Indicators.Item: Consistent v2 use by that app.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the legacy requirement; document; plan migration off v2.

TruePositive.Definition: A deliberate downgrade to bypass AMSI/script-block logging.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; open IR; rely on process/network telemetry for what ran.
Consider removing the PSv2 feature estate-wide.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured script pinning v2 unnecessarily.

Indicators.Item: A known script forcing v2 by habit.

SOCAction.Item: Update the script to a supported version; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
